hypotheses.statement: Invasive cancer spots at the tumor–lymphocyte interface show a higher basal-like epithelial program (KRT14/KRT5) relative to the luminal-like program (EPCAM/KRT8/KRT18) compared with invasive cancer spots located in the tumor core without lymphocyte neighbors.
hypotheses.rationale: OBSERVATION 4 and 9 indicate strong spatial interfaces between lymphocytes and invasive cancer, while OBSERVATION 6 shows distinct spatial patterning of basal versus luminal keratins within epithelial/tumor regions. If immune contact is associated with a more basal-like invasive phenotype at the edge, then invasive cancer spots abutting lymphocyte-classified spots should be relatively enriched for KRT14/KRT5 compared to EPCAM/KRT8/KRT18 versus invasive spots embedded in the tumor core.

contrasts.name: interface_invasive_vs_core_invasive
contrasts.group_1_definition: Spots with Classification == 'Invasive cancer + lymphocytes' whose spatial nearest neighbors (e.g., within a fixed-radius or kNN graph) include at least one spot with Classification == 'Lymphocytes'.
contrasts.group_2_definition: Spots with Classification == 'Invasive cancer + lymphocytes' whose nearest neighbors are all annotated as tumor-like (e.g., 'Invasive cancer + lymphocytes', DCIS) and include no spots with Classification == 'Lymphocytes'.

metrics.name: module_score_basal
metrics.description: Per-spot average normalized expression of KRT14 and KRT5.

metrics.name: module_score_luminal
metrics.description: Per-spot average normalized expression of EPCAM, KRT8, KRT18.

metrics.name: effect_size_difference
metrics.description: Difference in mean basal_minus_luminal between interface_invasive and core_invasive (and optionally Cohen's d).

metrics.name: p_value_rank_sum
metrics.description: Two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test comparing basal_minus_luminal between interface_invasive and core_invasive, with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction.

test_plan.decision_criteria: SUPPORT if interface_invasive spots have a significantly higher basal_minus_luminal score than core_invasive spots, defined as: (i) mean(basal_minus_luminal_interface) − mean(basal_minus_luminal_core) ≥ 0.15 on log-normalized scale, and (ii) FDR-adjusted p_value_rank_sum < 0.05. REFUTE if these conditions are not met or the direction is reversed (interface_invasive not more basal-biased than core_invasive).

group_size_criteria.fallback_strategy: If any comparison group has fewer than 20 spots, merge closely related classes within the same broad category (e.g., tumor core-like vs non-core) or simplify the contrast to interface vs non-interface spots.

qc_covariates.notes: Include QC metrics such as nCount_RNA and nFeature_RNA as covariates or perform sensitivity analyses with and without these covariates.

test_plan.notes: Phase 3 result: REFINE based on current dataset; see test_results_phase3.json for metrics.

hypotheses.statement: Lymphocyte-classified spots adjacent to invasive cancer (tumor-proximal aggregates) are relatively enriched for T cell markers compared to B cell markers, whereas lymphocyte spots embedded in stromal/normal territories are less T cell–biased or more B cell–balanced.
hypotheses.rationale: OBSERVATION 4 and 9 show that lymphocytes are frequently adjacent to invasive cancer regions, forming tumor–immune interfaces, while OBSERVATION 5 notes lymphocytes also occur in stromal domains. OBSERVATION 7 indicates that T cell (CD3D, CD3E, CD2) and B cell (MS4A1, CD79A) markers form discrete immune foci. A plausible implication is that tumor-associated immune aggregates are more T cell–dominated, whereas stromal lymphoid areas are more mixed or B cell–enriched. This predicts a higher T-vs-B marker bias in tumor-proximal lymphocyte spots than in stromal-associated lymphocyte spots.

contrasts.name: tumor_proximal_vs_stromal_lymphocytes
contrasts.group_1_definition: Spots with Classification == 'Lymphocytes' that have at least one neighbor with Classification in {'Invasive cancer + lymphocytes', 'DCIS'}.
contrasts.group_2_definition: Spots with Classification == 'Lymphocytes' whose neighbors do NOT include any 'Invasive cancer + lymphocytes' or 'DCIS' spots and instead are restricted to stromal/normal labels such as 'Stroma', 'Stroma + adipose tissue', 'Normal + stroma + lymphocytes'.

metrics.name: t_module_score
metrics.description: Per-spot average normalized expression of CD3D, CD3E, CD2.

metrics.name: b_module_score
metrics.description: Per-spot average normalized expression of MS4A1, CD79A.

metrics.name: t_minus_b_score
metrics.description: Difference t_module_score - b_module_score per lymphocyte spot.

metrics.name: effect_size_difference
metrics.description: Difference in mean t_minus_b_score between tumor_proximal_lymphocytes and stromal_lymphocytes (and optionally Cohen's d).

metrics.name: p_value_rank_sum
metrics.description: Two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test comparing t_minus_b_score between the two lymphocyte groups, with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction.

test_plan.decision_criteria: SUPPORT if tumor_proximal_lymphocytes have a significantly higher T-vs-B bias than stromal_lymphocytes, defined as: (i) mean(t_minus_b_score_tumor_proximal) − mean(t_minus_b_score_stromal) ≥ 0.1 on log-normalized scale, and (ii) FDR-adjusted p_value_rank_sum < 0.05. REFUTE if the difference does not reach this effect size or significance, or if stromal_lymphocytes show equal or greater T-cell bias.

group_size_criteria.fallback_strategy: If any comparison group has fewer than 20 spots, merge closely related classes within the same broad category (e.g., tumor core-like vs non-core) or simplify the contrast to interface vs non-interface spots.

test_plan.notes: Phase 3 result: DROPPED based on current dataset; see test_results_phase3.json for metrics.

hypotheses.statement: Spots at tumor–stroma interfaces are enriched for myeloid marker expression (LYZ, CD68) relative to both tumor-core and stroma-core spots, indicating preferential localization of myeloid cells at invasive fronts.
hypotheses.rationale: OBSERVATION 2 and 9 indicate that tumor and stromal classifications form coherent domains with clear interfaces, while OBSERVATION 5 describes broad stromal territories surrounding the invasive cancer core. OBSERVATION 8 shows that myeloid markers (LYZ, CD68) are expressed in punctate patterns overlapping stromal and immune-associated regions. If myeloid cells preferentially accumulate at the interface between tumor and stroma, interface spots—defined by mixed tumor and stroma neighbors—should show higher myeloid marker scores than either tumor-core or stroma-core spots.

groups.label: tumor_stroma_interface
groups.definition: Spots of any Classification whose neighbors include at least one tumor-like spot (e.g., 'Invasive cancer + lymphocytes' or 'DCIS') and at least one stromal-like spot (e.g., 'Stroma', 'Stroma + adipose tissue', 'Normal + stroma + lymphocytes').

groups.label: tumor_core
groups.definition: Spots with Classification in {'Invasive cancer + lymphocytes', 'DCIS'} whose neighbors are all tumor-like (same set) and include no stromal-like classifications.

groups.label: stroma_core
groups.definition: Spots with Classification in {'Stroma', 'Stroma + adipose tissue', 'Normal + stroma + lymphocytes'} whose neighbors are all stromal-like and include no tumor-like classifications.

metrics.name: myeloid_module_score
metrics.description: Per-spot average normalized expression of LYZ and CD68.

metrics.name: group_mean_scores
metrics.description: Mean myeloid_module_score in tumor_stroma_interface, tumor_core, and stroma_core.

metrics.name: kruskal_wallis_p
metrics.description: P-value from Kruskal–Wallis test comparing myeloid_module_score across the three groups.

metrics.name: pairwise_effect_sizes
metrics.description: Pairwise differences in mean myeloid_module_score (and optionally Cohen's d) for interface vs tumor_core and interface vs stroma_core, with BH-corrected pairwise Wilcoxon tests.

test_plan.decision_criteria: SUPPORT if: (i) Kruskal–Wallis test across the three groups yields p < 0.05, and (ii) tumor_stroma_interface has higher mean myeloid_module_score than both tumor_core and stroma_core by at least 0.1 log-normalized units, with FDR-adjusted pairwise p-values < 0.05 for both comparisons. REFUTE if these conditions are not satisfied or if either core group equals or exceeds interface myeloid scores.

group_size_criteria.fallback_strategy: If any comparison group has fewer than 20 spots, merge closely related classes within the same broad category (e.g., tumor core-like vs non-core) or simplify the contrast to interface vs non-interface spots.

hypotheses.statement: The spatial adjacency between lymphocyte-classified spots and invasive cancer regions is stronger than expected from shared localization to high-quality (high nCount_RNA / nFeature_RNA) tissue areas, i.e., the lymphocyte–tumor neighbor association remains significant after adjusting for QC gradients.
hypotheses.rationale: OBSERVATION 3 reports smooth spatial gradients in RNA counts and detected genes, with central dense tissue having higher QC metrics. OBSERVATION 4 and 9 show prominent spatial co-localization and neighbor associations between lymphocytes and invasive cancer regions. To rule out QC-driven artifacts (e.g., both lymphocytes and tumor occurring mainly in high-quality central areas), one can test whether lymphocyte–tumor adjacency remains enriched after accounting for nCount_RNA and nFeature_RNA.

inputs.neighbor_graph: precomputed spatial kNN or radius graph on adata.obsm['spatial']

contrasts.name: lymphocyte_neighbors_of_tumor_vs_expected
contrasts.definition: Model the probability that a spot is 'Lymphocytes' as a function of whether it neighbors invasive cancer (neighbors with Classification in {'Invasive cancer + lymphocytes', 'DCIS'}) while adjusting for QC metrics.

metrics.name: logistic_regression_coefficient
metrics.description: Coefficient (and standard error) for a binary indicator of having at least one invasive cancer neighbor in a logistic regression predicting whether a spot's Classification == 'Lymphocytes', including nCount_RNA and nFeature_RNA as covariates.

metrics.name: p_value_invasive_neighbor_effect
metrics.description: Wald test p-value (or likelihood ratio test p-value) for the invasive-neighbor coefficient, with BH correction if multiple models are fitted.

metrics.name: odds_ratio_invasive_neighbor
metrics.description: Exponentiated logistic regression coefficient giving the odds ratio of a spot being 'Lymphocytes' when it has at least one invasive cancer neighbor, adjusted for QC metrics.

test_plan.decision_criteria: SUPPORT if, in the adjusted logistic regression, the invasive-neighbor indicator has a positive coefficient corresponding to an odds_ratio_invasive_neighbor ≥ 1.5 and an FDR-adjusted p_value_invasive_neighbor_effect < 0.05. REFUTE if the adjusted association is non-significant (FDR ≥ 0.05) or weak (odds_ratio_invasive_neighbor < 1.5), indicating that QC gradients largely explain the observed adjacency.

group_size_criteria.fallback_strategy: If any comparison group has fewer than 20 spots, merge closely related classes within the same broad category (e.g., tumor core-like vs non-core) or simplify the contrast to interface vs non-interface spots.

qc_covariates.notes: Include QC metrics such as nCount_RNA and nFeature_RNA as covariates or perform sensitivity analyses with and without these covariates.
